Title: Antidiabetic and hypoglycemic effect of Nigella sativa seed extract in streptozotocin-induced diabetic rats
Abstract: The antidiabetic activity of Nigella sativa (black seed) was investigated in Wistar rats. The methanolic extract significantly lowered blood glucose and improved glycemic control. Phytochemical screening revealed thymoquinone as the major constituent.
Author Keywords: Nigella sativa; antidiabetic; thymoquinone; blood glucose
Authors with affiliations: Al-Rashidi H., Department of Pharmacology, King Saud University, Riyadh, Saudi Arabia

Title: Anticancer potential of Peganum harmala alkaloids against human breast cancer cell lines
Abstract: The cytotoxic and antiproliferative activity of Peganum harmala (Syrian rue) alkaloids was evaluated in vitro against MCF-7 cells. Harmine induced apoptosis with an IC50 of 18 ug/mL, indicating strong antitumor activity.
Author Keywords: Peganum harmala; anticancer; apoptosis; harmine; MCF-7
Authors with affiliations: Tazi A., Faculty of Sciences, Mohammed V University, Rabat, Morocco

Title: A systematic review and meta-analysis of Trigonella foenum-graecum (fenugreek) for glycemic control in type 2 diabetes
Abstract: This systematic review followed PRISMA guidelines. A random effects model pooled data from 12 randomized controlled trials. Fenugreek significantly reduced fasting blood glucose (pooled effect), confirming its antidiabetic role.
Authors with affiliations: Karimi M., School of Pharmacy, Tehran University of Medical Sciences, Tehran, Iran

Title: Ethnobotanical survey of medicinal plants used to treat cancer in southern Jordan
Abstract: An ethnobotanical survey documented plants used by traditional healers. Ziziphus spina-christi, Artemisia herba-alba and Peganum harmala were the most cited species for anticancer and anti-inflammatory use.
Author Keywords: ethnobotanical survey; Jordan; anticancer; traditional medicine
Authors with affiliations: Oran S., Department of Biological Sciences, University of Jordan, Amman, Jordan

Title: Antihypertensive and antioxidant activity of Hibiscus sabdariffa calyces: a randomized placebo-controlled clinical trial
Abstract: In this double blind placebo controlled clinical trial, healthy volunteers consuming Hibiscus sabdariffa (karkade) showed reduced blood pressure. The hypotensive and antioxidant effects were significant versus placebo.
Author Keywords: Hibiscus sabdariffa; antihypertensive; clinical trial; blood pressure
Authors with affiliations: Ahmed O., Faculty of Pharmacy, Cairo University, Cairo, Egypt

Title: Hepatoprotective effect of Silybum marianum against carbon tetrachloride induced liver damage
Abstract: The hepatoprotective activity of Silybum marianum (milk thistle) was investigated in albino mice. Silymarin reduced liver enzyme markers against CCl4-induced hepatotoxicity, confirming its liver protective role.
Authors with affiliations: Bouzid N., Faculty of Medicine, University of Tunis El Manar, Tunis, Tunisia

Title: Antimicrobial and antibiofilm activity of Thymus vulgaris essential oil against multidrug-resistant bacteria
Abstract: The antimicrobial activity of Thymus vulgaris (zaatar) essential oil was evaluated. Minimum inhibitory concentration values against Staphylococcus aureus confirmed strong antibacterial and antibiofilm effects.
Author Keywords: Thymus vulgaris; antimicrobial; essential oil; MIC
Authors with affiliations: Khalil R., Department of Biology, American University of Beirut, Beirut, Lebanon

Title: Curcuma longa (turmeric) curcumin in colorectal cancer: a narrative review
Abstract: This narrative review summarises the anticancer and anti-inflammatory mechanisms of curcumin from Curcuma longa. Evidence for antiproliferative and chemopreventive activity in colorectal cancer is discussed.
Authors with affiliations: Sharma P., Department of Oncology, All India Institute of Medical Sciences, New Delhi, India

Title: Neuroprotective and antidepressant effects of Crocus sativus (saffron) in a rat model
Abstract: The neuroprotective activity of Crocus sativus (saffron) was investigated. Crocin showed antidepressant and memory-enhancing effects, with acetylcholinesterase inhibitory activity in the treated group.
Authors with affiliations: Rahmani F., Faculty of Pharmacy, Mashhad University of Medical Sciences, Mashhad, Iran

Title: Wound healing activity of Aloe vera gel in diabetic foot ulcers: a case series
Abstract: We report a case series of diabetic foot ulcers treated with topical Aloe vera. Re-epithelialization and tissue regeneration were observed, supporting the wound healing and anti-inflammatory use of the plant.
Author Keywords: Aloe vera; wound healing; case series; diabetic foot
Authors with affiliations: Al-Maqtari M., Faculty of Medicine, Sana'a University, Sana'a, Yemen

Title: Antimalarial and antileishmanial activity of Artemisia herba-alba extracts
Abstract: The antiparasitic activity of Artemisia herba-alba (shih) was evaluated in vitro. The extract showed antiplasmodial and antileishmanial activity, supporting traditional antimalarial use in North Africa.
Authors with affiliations: Belkacem N., Laboratory of Natural Substances, University of Algiers, Algiers, Algeria

Title: Anti-inflammatory and anti-arthritic activity of Boswellia sacra frankincense resin
Abstract: The anti-inflammatory activity of Boswellia sacra (luban) was investigated. Boswellic acids reduced paw edema and showed anti-arthritic and immunomodulatory effects in the carrageenan-induced model.
Authors with affiliations: Al-Harrasi A., Natural and Medical Sciences Research Center, University of Nizwa, Nizwa, Oman

Title: Chemical composition and antioxidant capacity of Punica granatum peel from Turkey
Abstract: The antioxidant activity of Punica granatum (pomegranate) peel was determined using DPPH and FRAP assays. High radical scavenging and reducing power were recorded, correlating with total phenolic content.
Authors with affiliations: Yilmaz H., Department of Food Engineering, Ege University, Izmir, Turkey

Title: Ginkgo biloba extract for cognitive decline: a systematic review
Abstract: A systematic review of randomized controlled trials assessed Ginkgo biloba for cognitive decline. The neuroprotective evidence was heterogeneous across studies following a systematic search.
Author Keywords: Ginkgo biloba; systematic review; cognition; neuroprotective
Authors with affiliations: Weber K., Institute of Neurology, University of Munich, Munich, Germany

Title: Editorial: the growing role of Middle Eastern medicinal plants in drug discovery
Abstract: This editorial reflects on the pharmacological promise of regional flora and calls for standardized ethnopharmacological reporting across the MENA region.
Authors with affiliations: Nasser A., Faculty of Pharmacy, University of Baghdad, Baghdad, Iraq

Title: Gastroprotective and antiulcer activity of Glycyrrhiza glabra root extract in rats
Abstract: The gastroprotective activity of Glycyrrhiza glabra (licorice) was evaluated. The aqueous extract reduced gastric lesions and showed antiulcer and anti-inflammatory effects against ethanol-induced ulcers.
Authors with affiliations: Mansour L., Department of Pharmacology, King Abdulaziz University, Jeddah, Saudi Arabia

Title: Antidiabetic and antihyperlipidemic effect of Teucrium polium in alloxan-induced diabetic rabbits
Abstract: The antidiabetic and hypolipidemic activity of Teucrium polium (jaadeh) was investigated. The extract lowered blood glucose and improved lipid profile, showing antioxidant activity in diabetic rabbits.
Authors with affiliations: Haddad F., Faculty of Medicine, University of Damascus, Damascus, Syria

Title: Cytotoxic and apoptotic effects of Rhazya stricta leaf extract on hepatocellular carcinoma cells
Abstract: The anticancer activity of Rhazya stricta (harmal) was evaluated in vitro against HepG2 cells. The extract was cytotoxic and pro-apoptotic, indicating antitumor and antiproliferative potential.
Authors with affiliations: Bin Sabt J., Department of Biochemistry, United Arab Emirates University, Al Ain, United Arab Emirates
